## claude.ai entire-prod-us
Entire MCP — an investigation surface over Entire's engineering data: repos and their analytics, git history (commits, files, trees, refs, diffs), the AI checkpoints and sessions behind the code (with transcripts and token accounting), trails (PR-like change proposals), and code search. Reads are curated `*_entire` tools; a small write/ops group covers trail/review/runner/dispatch mutations.

Workflow: when you only have a repo name, path, or URL, call resolve_entire_repo first, then pass the repo it returns to repo-scoped tools. Prefer the aggregation tools (get_entire_repo_overview, get_entire_my_activity) over hand-rolling stats from raw listings.

Querying conventions (shared by every tool):
- Addressing: name a repo by a prefixed path (gh/<owner>/<repo>, et/<project>/<repo>, git/<owner>/<repo>) or a repo ULID. Repo ULIDs are REGION-SCOPED — the same repo has a different ULID per region, so never carry a ULID across regions or sessions; if a tool rejects one, re-resolve with resolve_entire_repo.
- Pagination: every list takes an opaque cursor and returns next_cursor when more remains — exhaust the pages before concluding "that's all".
- Time: since/until are ISO 8601 / RFC3339 bounds; where offered, timeframe is a relative window (last-month, last-3-months, last-6-months).
- Size: reads that can be large (files, diffs, transcripts) honor max_tokens and return next_cursor to continue — raise max_tokens or page rather than assuming truncation is the whole story.

Pitfalls:
- sessions[].tokenUsage on a checkpoint is a PER-CHECKPOINT delta, not a session total — sum across a session's checkpoints, or use get_entire_session for the authoritative total.
- list_entire_checkpoints silently truncates older history; for a branch's COMPLETE checkpoint membership, paginate list_entire_commits and collect the per-commit checkpoint IDs.

+// MetadataDenyRule is the Read deny rule Entire used to install into agent
+// permission configs to keep an agent from reading `.entire/metadata`.
+//
+// It is no longer installed, and `entire enable` and `entire doctor` remove it.
+// The constant survives because removing it is now the migration, so the exact
+// string still has to be recognisable — and because it is what identifies the
+// rule as ours: a rule byte-identical to this one was written by Entire, so
+// deleting it takes nothing the user chose.
+//
+// Why it went, in order of weight:
+//
+//   - A `deny` rule is a hard block, not a hint. Rules resolve deny → ask →
+//     allow, first match wins, and a deny rule cannot carry allowlist
+//     exceptions, so there is no way to soften it. Claude Code applies Read
+//     deny rules to file-reading Bash commands too, so a recursive grep from
+//     the repo root — or a command that merely names the path — is refused and
+//     has to be approved by hand. That defeats unattended/auto permission
+//     modes for a whole class of ordinary commands.
+//   - It guarded a staging buffer, not a store. `.entire/metadata/<session>`
+//     holds a `full.jsonl` that is rewritten from the agent's own transcript on
+//     every Stop and deleted once the session is condensed. The durable copy
+//     lives in the checkpoint tree, which no permission rule covers: the same
+//     transcript is readable with `git show entire/checkpoints/v1:...`.
+//   - It was mostly redundant. `.entire/.gitignore` already ignores
+//     `metadata/`, and Claude Code's Grep skips gitignored files, so the
+//     accidental-bulk-read case that motivated the rule was already covered.
+//     Glob does not respect gitignore, but Glob returns names, not content.
+//
+// Deliberately NOT replaced with a PreToolUse hook on Read: that fires a
+// subprocess for every file the agent reads, on a hook path that is already the
+// dominant cost of a turn.
+const MetadataDenyRule = "Read(./.entire/metadata/**)"
+
+// HasMetadataDenyRule reports whether rawPermissions still carries the retired
+// metadata deny rule. Used by the diagnostics that tell a user why they are
+// being asked to approve ordinary commands; it does not mutate anything.
+func HasMetadataDenyRule(rawPermissions map[string]json.RawMessage) bool {
+	rules, ok := denyRules(rawPermissions)
+	if !ok {
+		return false
+	}
+	return slices.Contains(rules, MetadataDenyRule)
+}
+
+// RemoveMetadataDenyRule drops the retired metadata deny rule from
+// rawPermissions, mutating it in place, and reports whether anything changed.
+//
+// Only the exact MetadataDenyRule string is removed, so every other deny rule —
+// including one a user wrote — is preserved. An empty `deny` array is deleted
+// rather than left behind, so a config Entire fully owned goes back to holding
+// no permissions block at all instead of an empty one.
+//
+// A `deny` value that will not parse as a string array is left untouched: it is
+// not ours, and rewriting what we cannot read is worse than leaving it.
+func RemoveMetadataDenyRule(rawPermissions map[string]json.RawMessage) (bool, error) {
+	rules, ok := denyRules(rawPermissions)
+	if !ok {
+		return false, nil
+	}
+	kept := make([]string, 0, len(rules))
+	for _, rule := range rules {
+		if rule != MetadataDenyRule {
+			kept = append(kept, rule)
+		}
+	}
+	if len(kept) == len(rules) {
+		return false, nil
+	}
+	if len(kept) == 0 {
+		delete(rawPermissions, "deny")
+		return true, nil
+	}
+	denyJSON, err := json.Marshal(kept)
+	if err != nil {
+		return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal permissions.deny: %w", err)
+	}
+	rawPermissions["deny"] = denyJSON
+	return true, nil
+}
+
+// denyRules parses rawPermissions["deny"] as a string array. ok is false when
+// the key is absent or holds something else, which both mean "nothing here for
+// us to act on".
+func denyRules(rawPermissions map[string]json.RawMessage) (rules []string, ok bool) {
+	denyRaw, present := rawPermissions["deny"]
+	if !present {
+		return nil, false
+	}
+	if err := json.Unmarshal(denyRaw, &rules); err != nil {
+		return nil, false
+	}
+	return rules, true
+}
+
+// PermissionConfigOwner is implemented by an agent that keeps Entire-managed
+// entries in a JSON config with a top-level "permissions" object. It exists so
+// the shared diagnostics and the retired-rule migration can inspect and repair
+// that block without knowing where each agent keeps its config.
+//
+// Implemented by Claude Code (.claude/settings.json) and Factory AI Droid
+// (.factory/settings.json) — the two agents Entire ever wrote MetadataDenyRule
+// into.
+type PermissionConfigOwner interface {
+	// PermissionConfig returns the agent's permission-bearing config file for
+	// the current worktree. It does not create anything.
+	PermissionConfig(ctx context.Context) (*HookConfigFile, error)
+}
+
+// AsPermissionConfigOwner returns ag as a PermissionConfigOwner when it keeps a
+// permissions block Entire may have written into.
+func AsPermissionConfigOwner(ag Agent) (PermissionConfigOwner, bool) {
+	owner, ok := ag.(PermissionConfigOwner)
+	return owner, ok
+}
+
+// HasRetiredMetadataDenyRule reports whether ag's config still carries the
+// retired deny rule. It is read-only and answers false for every reason that is
+// not a positive sighting — agent doesn't own a permissions config, file absent,
+// unreadable, or unparseable — because its only callers are diagnostics, and
+// telling a user their config is broken on the strength of a failed read is
+// worse than staying quiet.
+func HasRetiredMetadataDenyRule(ctx context.Context, ag Agent) bool {
+	owner, ok := AsPermissionConfigOwner(ag)
+	if !ok {
+		return false
+	}
+	cfg, err := owner.PermissionConfig(ctx)
+	if err != nil || !cfg.Exists() {
+		return false
+	}
+	_, rawPermissions, err := readPermissionsBlock(cfg)
+	if err != nil {
+		return false
+	}
+	return HasMetadataDenyRule(rawPermissions)
+}
+
+// RepairRetiredMetadataDenyRule removes the retired deny rule from ag's config
+// and reports whether the file was changed.
+//
+// Unlike the detector above, this one returns its errors: it is reached from
+// `entire doctor`, where a config that cannot be parsed is the answer the user
+// needs rather than something to swallow.
+func RepairRetiredMetadataDenyRule(ctx context.Context, ag Agent) (bool, error) {
+	owner, ok := AsPermissionConfigOwner(ag)
+	if !ok {
+		return false, nil
+	}
+	cfg, err := owner.PermissionConfig(ctx)
+	if err != nil {
+		return false, err //nolint:wrapcheck // the agent's accessor already names its file
+	}
+	if !cfg.Exists() {
+		return false, nil
+	}
+	rawSettings, rawPermissions, err := readPermissionsBlock(cfg)
+	if err != nil {
+		return false, err
+	}
+	changed, err := RemoveMetadataDenyRule(rawPermissions)
+	if err != nil || !changed {
+		return false, err
+	}
+
+	// An emptied permissions block is deleted rather than written back as {}, so
+	// a config Entire fully owned ends up as it was before Entire touched it.
+	if len(rawPermissions) == 0 {
+		delete(rawSettings, "permissions")
+	} else {
+		permJSON, marshalErr := jsonutil.MarshalWithNoHTMLEscape(rawPermissions)
+		if marshalErr != nil {
+			return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal permissions for %s: %w", cfg.Path(), marshalErr)
+		}
+		rawSettings["permissions"] = permJSON
+	}
+
+	output, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(rawSettings, "", "  ")
+	if err != nil {
+		return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal %s: %w", cfg.Path(), err)
+	}
+	if err := cfg.Write(output, 0o600); err != nil {
+		return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to write %s: %w", cfg.Path(), err)
+	}
+	return true, nil
+}
+
+// readPermissionsBlock reads cfg and returns its top-level fields plus the
+// "permissions" object. rawPermissions is always non-nil so callers can index
+// it without a nil check.
+func readPermissionsBlock(cfg *HookConfigFile) (rawSettings, rawPermissions map[string]json.RawMessage, err error) {
+	data, err := cfg.Read()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read %s: %w", cfg.Path(), err)
+	}
+	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &rawSettings); err != nil {
+		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse %s: %w", cfg.Path(), err)
+	}
+	if rawSettings == nil {
+		rawSettings = make(map[string]json.RawMessage)
+	}
+	if permRaw, ok := rawSettings["permissions"]; ok {
+		if err := json.Unmarshal(permRaw, &rawPermissions); err != nil {
+			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse permissions in %s: %w", cfg.Path(), err)
+		}
+	}
+	if rawPermissions == nil {
+		rawPermissions = make(map[string]json.RawMessage)
+	}
+	return rawSettings, rawPermissions, nil
+}

164	// installHookEntries mutates rawHooks in place to ensure every Entire hook is
165	// present, migrating stale entries (from older CLI versions or, when force is
166	// set, any current Entire hook) first. Returns the number of hooks newly
167	// added and whether any stale entry was dropped (see the staleDropped comment
168	// at its InstallHooks call site for why that forces a write on its own).
169	func installHookEntries(rawHooks map[string]json.RawMessage, force bool) (count int, staleDropped bool) {
170		var preToolUse, postToolUse []ClaudeHookMatcher
171		parseHookType(rawHooks, "PreToolUse", &preToolUse)
172		parseHookType(rawHooks, "PostToolUse", &postToolUse)
173	
174		// The "simple" hook types all share one shape: a single Entire command
175		// under an empty-string matcher, no tool-use targeting. Handling them
176		// data-driven (rather than one parse/strip/add/marshal block per type)
177		// keeps this function's complexity from growing linearly with each new
178		// simple hook type Entire registers.
179		simpleHooks := []struct {
180			hookType string
181			command  string
182		}{
183			{"SessionStart", agent.WrapProductionJSONWarningHookCommand("entire hooks claude-code session-start", agent.WarningFormatMultiLine)},
184			{"SessionEnd", agent.WrapProductionSilentHookCommand("entire hooks claude-code session-end")},
185			{"Stop", agent.WrapProductionSilentHookCommand("entire hooks claude-code stop")},
186			{"SubagentStop", agent.WrapProductionSilentHookCommand("entire hooks claude-code subagent-stop")},
187			{"UserPromptSubmit", agent.WrapProductionSilentHookCommand("entire hooks claude-code user-prompt-submit")},
188		}
189		simpleMatchers := make(map[string][]ClaudeHookMatcher, len(simpleHooks))
190		for _, h := range simpleHooks {
191			var m []ClaudeHookMatcher
192			parseHookType(rawHooks, h.hookType, &m)
193			simpleMatchers[h.hookType] = m
194		}
195	
196		// If force is true, remove all existing Entire hooks first
197		if force {
198			for _, h := range simpleHooks {
199				simpleMatchers[h.hookType] = removeEntireHooks(simpleMatchers[h.hookType])
200			}
201			preToolUse = removeEntireHooksFromMatchers(preToolUse)
202			postToolUse = removeEntireHooksFromMatchers(postToolUse)
203		}
204	
205		// Define tool-use hook commands (the simple hooks' commands live in
206		// simpleHooks above).
207		preTaskCmd := agent.WrapProductionSilentHookCommand("entire hooks claude-code pre-task")
208		postTaskCmd := agent.WrapProductionSilentHookCommand("entire hooks claude-code post-task")
209		postTodoCmd := agent.WrapProductionSilentHookCommand("entire hooks claude-code post-todo")
210	
211		// Drop Entire hooks left by older versions before adding the current ones,
212		// so a stale command (e.g. the removed local-dev launcher, which ran a
213		// script inside the working tree) does not survive alongside them.
214		// Unconditional: a plain `entire enable` must migrate too, not just --force.
215		drop := func(matchers []ClaudeHookMatcher, want ...string) []ClaudeHookMatcher {
216			out, dropped := dropStaleEntireHooks(matchers, want...)
217			if dropped {
218				staleDropped = true
219			}
220			return out
221		}
222		for _, h := range simpleHooks {
223			simpleMatchers[h.hookType] = drop(simpleMatchers[h.hookType], h.command)
224		}
225		preToolUse = drop(preToolUse, preTaskCmd)
226		postToolUse = drop(postToolUse, postTaskCmd, postTodoCmd)
227	
228		// Add hooks if they don't exist
229		for _, h := range simpleHooks {
230			m := simpleMatchers[h.hookType]
231			if !hookCommandExists(m, h.command) {
232				simpleMatchers[h.hookType] = addHookToMatcher(m, "", h.command)
233				count++
234			}
235		}
236		if !hookCommandExistsWithMatcher(preToolUse, subagentToolMatcher, preTaskCmd) {
237			preToolUse = addHookToMatcher(preToolUse, subagentToolMatcher, preTaskCmd)
238			count++
239		}
240		if !hookCommandExistsWithMatcher(postToolUse, subagentToolMatcher, postTaskCmd) {
241			postToolUse = addHookToMatcher(postToolUse, subagentToolMatcher, postTaskCmd)
242			count++
243		}
244		if !hookCommandExistsWithMatcher(postToolUse, taskToolMatcher, postTodoCmd) {
245			postToolUse = addHookToMatcher(postToolUse, taskToolMatcher, postTodoCmd)
246			count++
247		}
248	
249		// Marshal modified hook types back to rawHooks
250		for _, h := range simpleHooks {
251			marshalHookType(rawHooks, h.hookType, simpleMatchers[h.hookType])
252		}
253		marshalHookType(rawHooks, "PreToolUse", preToolUse)
254		marshalHookType(rawHooks, "PostToolUse", postToolUse)
255	
256		return count, staleDropped
257	}

308	// UninstallHooks removes Entire hooks from Claude Code settings.
309	func (c *ClaudeCodeAgent) UninstallHooks(ctx context.Context) error {
310		cfg, err := claudeHookConfig(ctx)
311		if err != nil {
312			return err
313		}
314		data, err := cfg.Read()
315		if err != nil {
316			// Same split AreHooksInstalled makes: an absent file is an answer, an
317			// unreadable one is not. Collapsing both to "nothing to uninstall" leaves
318			// the hooks on disk and reports success, which is what uninstall is
319			// supposed to stop doing.
320			if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
321				return nil
322			}
323			return fmt.Errorf("read %s: %w", cfg.Path(), err)
324		}
325	
326		var rawSettings map[string]json.RawMessage
327		if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &rawSettings); err != nil {
328			return fmt.Errorf("failed to parse settings.json: %w", err)
329		}
330	
331		// rawHooks preserves unknown hook types (e.g., "Notification")
332		var rawHooks map[string]json.RawMessage
333		if hooksRaw, ok := rawSettings["hooks"]; ok {
334			if err := json.Unmarshal(hooksRaw, &rawHooks); err != nil {
335				return fmt.Errorf("failed to parse hooks: %w", err)
336			}
337		}
338		if rawHooks == nil {
339			rawHooks = make(map[string]json.RawMessage)
340		}
341	
342		// Parse only the hook types we need to modify
343		var sessionStart, sessionEnd, stop, subagentStop, userPromptSubmit, preToolUse, postToolUse []ClaudeHookMatcher
344		parseHookType(rawHooks, "SessionStart", &sessionStart)
345		parseHookType(rawHooks, "SessionEnd", &sessionEnd)
346		parseHookType(rawHooks, "Stop", &stop)
347		parseHookType(rawHooks, "SubagentStop", &subagentStop)
348		parseHookType(rawHooks, "UserPromptSubmit", &userPromptSubmit)
349		parseHookType(rawHooks, "PreToolUse", &preToolUse)
350		parseHookType(rawHooks, "PostToolUse", &postToolUse)
351	
352		// Remove Entire hooks from all hook types
353		sessionStart = removeEntireHooks(sessionStart)
354		sessionEnd = removeEntireHooks(sessionEnd)
355		stop = removeEntireHooks(stop)
356		subagentStop = removeEntireHooks(subagentStop)
357		userPromptSubmit = removeEntireHooks(userPromptSubmit)
358		preToolUse = removeEntireHooksFromMatchers(preToolUse)
359		postToolUse = removeEntireHooksFromMatchers(postToolUse)
360	
361		// Marshal modified hook types back to rawHooks
362		marshalHookType(rawHooks, "SessionStart", sessionStart)
363		marshalHookType(rawHooks, "SessionEnd", sessionEnd)
364		marshalHookType(rawHooks, "Stop", stop)
365		marshalHookType(rawHooks, "SubagentStop", subagentStop)
366		marshalHookType(rawHooks, "UserPromptSubmit", userPromptSubmit)
367		marshalHookType(rawHooks, "PreToolUse", preToolUse)
368		marshalHookType(rawHooks, "PostToolUse", postToolUse)
369	
370		// Also remove the metadata deny rule from permissions
371		var rawPermissions map[string]json.RawMessage
372		if permRaw, ok := rawSettings["permissions"]; ok {
373			if err := json.Unmarshal(permRaw, &rawPermissions); err != nil {
374				// If parsing fails, just skip permissions cleanup
375				rawPermissions = nil
376			}
377		}
378	
379		if rawPermissions != nil {
380			// Same removal InstallHooks now performs; a marshal failure here leaves
381			// the rule in place, which uninstall reports through the write below
382			// rather than aborting the rest of the hook removal.
383			_, _ = agent.RemoveMetadataDenyRule(rawPermissions) //nolint:errcheck // best-effort during uninstall; hook removal must still complete
384	
385			// If permissions is empty, remove it entirely
386			if len(rawPermissions) > 0 {
387				permJSON, err := jsonutil.MarshalWithNoHTMLEscape(rawPermissions)
388				if err == nil {
389					rawSettings["permissions"] = permJSON
390				}
391			} else {
392				delete(rawSettings, "permissions")
393			}
394		}
395	
396		// Marshal hooks back (preserving unknown hook types)
397		if len(rawHooks) > 0 {
398			hooksJSON, err := jsonutil.MarshalWithNoHTMLEscape(rawHooks)
399			if err != nil {
400				return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal hooks: %w", err)
401			}
402			rawSettings["hooks"] = hooksJSON
403		} else {
404			delete(rawSettings, "hooks")
405		}
406	
407		// Write back
408		output, err := jsonutil.MarshalIndentWithNewline(rawSettings, "", "  ")
409		if err != nil {
410			return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal settings: %w", err)
411		}
412		return cfg.Write(output, 0o600) //nolint:wrapcheck // agent.HookConfigFile already names the file in its error
413	}

441	}

484	// CheckHookConfig reports whether Entire's Claude Code hooks are absent,
485	// current, or outdated. It is a read-only diagnostic used by `entire status`
486	// and `entire doctor`; it never modifies settings. Outdated is detected on the
487	// positive spec: Entire is installed (Stop hook present) yet one of the current
488	// tool-use matchers does not carry its Entire hook.
489	func CheckHookConfig(ctx context.Context) HookConfigState {
490		settings, err := loadClaudeSettings(ctx)
491		// An unreadable or malformed settings file collapses to HooksAbsent
492		// deliberately. This is a coarse three-state diagnostic for `entire status`
493		// and `entire doctor`, and no caller here acts on "could not tell" —
494		// AreHooksInstalled is the API that propagates that distinction to callers
495		// which must (e.g. uninstall deciding whether hooks can be left alone).
496		// loadClaudeSettings has already logged the failure.
497		if err != nil || !hasEntireHook(settings.Hooks.Stop) {
498			return HooksAbsent
499		}
500		subagentTools := splitMatcherTools(subagentToolMatcher)
501		taskTools := splitMatcherTools(taskToolMatcher)
502		if !hasEntireHookCoveringTools(settings.Hooks.PreToolUse, subagentTools) ||
503			!hasEntireHookCoveringTools(settings.Hooks.PostToolUse, subagentTools) ||
504			!hasEntireHookCoveringTools(settings.Hooks.PostToolUse, taskTools) ||
505			!hasEntireHook(settings.Hooks.SubagentStop) {
506			return HooksOutdated
507		}
508		return HooksCurrent
509	}

535	// splitMatcherTools splits a Claude Code tool matcher into its exact tool
536	// names. Matchers that InstallHooks writes are `|`-separated lists (Claude Code
537	// also accepts `,`); whitespace around separators is ignored. Returns the tools
538	// in order, dropping empties.
539	func splitMatcherTools(matcher string) []string {
540		parts := strings.FieldsFunc(matcher, func(r rune) bool { return r == '|' || r == ',' })
541		tools := make([]string, 0, len(parts))
542		for _, p := range parts {
543			if t := strings.TrimSpace(p); t != "" {
544				tools = append(tools, t)
545			}
546		}
547		return tools
548	}

550	// hasEntireHookCoveringTools reports whether an Entire hook is installed under a
551	// matcher that covers every tool in want. A widened matcher still counts: a
552	// matcher of "TaskCreate|TaskUpdate|TaskGet" covers {TaskCreate, TaskUpdate},
553	// so users who broaden a matcher aren't falsely flagged as outdated.
554	func hasEntireHookCoveringTools(matchers []ClaudeHookMatcher, want []string) bool {
555		for _, matcher := range matchers {
556			have := splitMatcherTools(matcher.Matcher)
557			coversAll := true
558			for _, w := range want {
559				if !slices.Contains(have, w) {
560					coversAll = false
561					break
562				}
563			}
564			if !coversAll {
565				continue
566			}
567			for _, hook := range matcher.Hooks {
568				if isEntireHook(hook.Command) {
569					return true
570				}
571			}
572		}
573		return false
574	}

580					if hook.Command == command {
581						return true
582					}
583				}
584			}
585		}

589	// addHookToMatcher appends command to the matcher named matcherName, creating it
590	// if absent. No timeout is set: Timeout exists on ClaudeHookEntry to round-trip
591	// settings files that carry one, but Entire's own hooks all keep Claude Code's
592	// default. (The removed local-dev mode was the only thing that needed a longer
593	// SessionEnd budget, because it compiled the CLI from source.)
594	func addHookToMatcher(matchers []ClaudeHookMatcher, matcherName, command string) []ClaudeHookMatcher {
595		entry := ClaudeHookEntry{
596			Type:    "command",
597			Command: command,
598		}
599	
600		// If no matcher name, add to a matcher with empty string
601		if matcherName == "" {
602			for i, matcher := range matchers {
603				if matcher.Matcher == "" {
604					matchers[i].Hooks = append(matchers[i].Hooks, entry)
605					return matchers
606				}
607			}
608			return append(matchers, ClaudeHookMatcher{
609				Matcher: "",
610				Hooks:   []ClaudeHookEntry{entry},
611			})
612		}
613	
614		// Find or create matcher with the given name
615		for i, matcher := range matchers {
616			if matcher.Matcher == matcherName {
617				matchers[i].Hooks = append(matchers[i].Hooks, entry)
618				return matchers
619			}
620		}
621	
622		return append(matchers, ClaudeHookMatcher{
623			Matcher: matcherName,
624			Hooks:   []ClaudeHookEntry{entry},
625		})
626	}

633	// dropStaleEntireHooks removes Entire-owned hooks whose command is not one of
634	// want, per matcher, pruning matchers left with no hooks. want is a set because
635	// one hook list can hold several Entire commands (PostToolUse carries both
636	// post-task and post-todo). See agent.DropStaleManagedHooks for why this runs on
637	// every install and why the dropped flag matters.
638	func dropStaleEntireHooks(matchers []ClaudeHookMatcher, want ...string) ([]ClaudeHookMatcher, bool) {
639		result := make([]ClaudeHookMatcher, 0, len(matchers))
640		dropped := false
641		for _, matcher := range matchers {
642			kept, d := agent.DropStaleManagedHooks(matcher.Hooks, hookEntryCommand, want)
643			if d {
644				dropped = true
645			}
646			if len(kept) > 0 {
647				matcher.Hooks = kept
648				result = append(result, matcher)
649			}
650		}
651		if !dropped {
652			return matchers, false
653		}
654		return result, true
655	}

14	// HookConfigFile is an agent's hook-configuration file inside the worktree —
15	// .claude/settings.json, .cursor/hooks.json, .gemini/settings.json,
16	// .github/hooks/entire.json, .factory/settings.json, .codex/hooks.json,
17	// .opencode/plugin/entire.ts.
18	//
19	// Seven agents each carried the same four lines: filepath.Join a repo root with
20	// a fixed relative path, then os.ReadFile / os.MkdirAll / os.WriteFile /
21	// os.Remove on the result, each with a //nolint:gosec saying the path came from
22	// the repo root. That justification is about where the path was BUILT and says
23	// nothing about where it RESOLVES, which is the part that matters: `.claude` and
24	// its siblings live in the working tree, and a working tree arrives by clone.
25	// A repository carrying a checked-in symlink at `.claude` therefore had
26	// `entire enable` create directories and write JSON through it, to wherever it
27	// pointed — outside the repository included.
28	//
29	// Anchoring on worktreedir fixes that at the root rather than at each call site:
30	// the base is the worktree root, the agent's fixed subpath is a NAME inside it,
31	// and directories are created with MkdirAllNoSymlink so a symlinked component is
32	// refused by name instead of silently followed. It also collapses the seven
33	// copies into one, which is what keeps the next agent integration from
34	// reintroducing the pattern.
35	//
36	// Every symlink component is refused, including the file itself. os.Root blocks
37	// a link that escapes the worktree but follows one pointing elsewhere inside
38	// it; accepting the leaf would let `.claude/settings.json -> ../victim.json`
39	// redirect both the merge read and the subsequent write.
40	//
41	// An earlier revision of this type deliberately allowed a symlinked leaf, on the
42	// grounds that pointing `.claude/settings.json` at a dotfile repo is a real
43	// setup Entire has no business breaking. That was reconsidered, and the reason
44	// is worth keeping: the merge READ pulls the target's contents into what Entire
45	// then writes, and the write is a rename, which replaces the user's link with a
46	// regular file rather than following it. Both happen silently. Refusing is the
47	// legible version of the same outcome.

49	// The setup still works, because the thing that makes a link dangerous here is
50	// that it arrived with the checkout. A developer who wants one keeps it out of
51	// the repository — `git rm --cached .claude/settings.json` and a .gitignore
52	// entry — and manages it locally, which is what a dotfile workflow does anyway.

60	//
61	// relPath is slash-separated and relative to the worktree root
62	// (".cursor/hooks.json"). The directory does not need to exist: Read reports a
63	// missing file the way os.ReadFile does, and Write creates the parents.
64	func OpenHookConfig(worktreeRoot, relPath string) (*HookConfigFile, error) {
65		name, err := worktreedir.Name(worktreeRoot, relPath)
66		if err != nil {
67			return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve hook config path: %w", err)
68		}
69		root, err := worktreedir.OpenAt(worktreeRoot)
70		if err != nil {
71			return nil, fmt.Errorf("open worktree root: %w", err)
72		}
73		return &HookConfigFile{
74			root: root,
75			name: name,
76			path: filepath.Join(worktreeRoot, filepath.FromSlash(name)),
77		}, nil
78	}

81	// has to name it. It is not an invitation to do I/O on the result.

84	// Read returns the file's contents. A missing file is reported unwrapped so
85	// callers can classify it with os.IsNotExist, which is how every agent's
86	// install path decides between "merge into existing" and "write fresh".
87	func (f *HookConfigFile) Read() ([]byte, error) {
88		return osroot.ReadFileNoFollow(f.root, f.name) //nolint:wrapcheck // see doc comment
89	}

92	//
93	// A symlinked parent directory counts as absent rather than as an error, since
94	// the signature has nowhere to put one. That is the useful answer: every caller
95	// uses this to choose between merging into an existing file and writing a fresh
96	// one, and Write refuses the same path with a message that names the link.
97	func (f *HookConfigFile) Exists() bool {
98		info, err := osroot.LstatNoSymlinks(f.root, f.name)
99		return err == nil && info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink == 0
100	}

102	// Write writes data, creating parent directories. A parent that already exists
103	// as a symlink is refused with osroot.ErrSymlinkedPath rather than followed.
104	func (f *HookConfigFile) Write(data []byte, perm os.FileMode) error {
105		if dir := path.Dir(f.name); dir != "." {
106			if err := osroot.MkdirAllNoSymlink(f.root, dir, 0o750); err != nil {
107				return fmt.Errorf("create %s: %w", path.Dir(f.path), err)
108			}
109		}
110		if info, err := osroot.LstatNoSymlinks(f.root, f.name); err == nil && info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {

112		} else if err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
113			return fmt.Errorf("write %s: %w", f.path, err)
114		}
115		if err := jsonutil.WriteFileAtomicIn(f.root, f.name, data, perm); err != nil {
116			return fmt.Errorf("write %s: %w", f.path, err)
117		}
118		return nil
119	}

122	// symlinked parent directory is, because the file this would delete is at the
123	// far end of a link Entire did not create.
124	func (f *HookConfigFile) Remove() error {
125		if err := osroot.RemoveNoSymlinks(f.root, f.name); err != nil {
126			return fmt.Errorf("remove %s: %w", f.path, err)
127		}
128		return nil

### 1. `clearFilesystemTranscript` duplicates `clearFilesystemPrompt`'s structure verbatim, and its own inline legacy-name construction bypasses the naming helper the same commit just wrote

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:1601-1645`

```go
func clearFilesystemPrompt(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) {
	root, err := entiredir.OpenForRead(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return
	}
	_ = osroot.RemoveNoSymlinks(root, sessionPromptName(sessionID)) //nolint:errcheck // ...
}
...
func clearFilesystemTranscript(ctx context.Context, sessionID string) {
	root, err := entiredir.OpenForRead(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return
	}
	_ = osroot.RemoveNoSymlinks(root, sessionTranscriptName(sessionID)) //nolint:errcheck // ...
	legacy := entiredir.MustName(paths.SessionMetadataDirFromSessionID(sessionID)) + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileNameLegacy
	_ = osroot.RemoveNoSymlinks(root, legacy) //nolint:errcheck // ...
}
```

**Cost:** The open-root-and-guard boilerplate (`entiredir.OpenForRead` + nil-check-and-return) is copied wholesale for the second function in the same file, rather than factoring "open the `.entire` root once, then remove one or more names" into one shared step. Worse, `clearFilesystemTranscript` builds the legacy path with a raw `entiredir.MustName(paths.SessionMetadataDirFromSessionID(sessionID)) + "/" + paths.TranscriptFileNameLegacy` expression instead of using the exact `sessionXName(sessionID)` naming-helper pattern that `sessionPromptName` (line 1596) and `sessionTranscriptName` (line 1611) — two functions above it, in the same diff — already established. The same one-line pattern now exists three times: as `sessionPromptName`, as `sessionTranscriptName`, and inlined a third time for the legacy name.

**Fix:** Add `sessionTranscriptNameLegacy(sessionID string) string` alongside `sessionTranscriptName` (matching the existing naming convention), and factor the open-root-and-remove step into one small helper (e.g. `removeSessionMetadataFile(ctx context.Context, name string)`) that `clearFilesystemPrompt` and `clearFilesystemTranscript` both call, with `clearFilesystemTranscript` calling it twice. Confirmed no pre-existing generic "remove one or more names under an already-opened root" helper exists in `cmd/entire/cli/osroot/osroot.go` (only bare `Remove`/`RemoveNoSymlinks`) or `cmd/entire/cli/entiredir/`, so this is sibling duplication introduced within the same change, not a miss of a utility that already existed elsewhere.

### 2. `TestInstallHooks_DropsEmptyDenyArray` reimplements the file's own `readPermissions` test helper

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/hooks_test.go:132-167`

The new test hand-rolls exactly what `readPermissions(t, tempDir)` (defined lower in the same file, at line 255) already does — read `.claude/settings.json`, unmarshal the top level, pull out `"permissions"`:

```go
settingsPath := filepath.Join(tempDir, ".claude", "settings.json")
data, err := os.ReadFile(settingsPath)
...
var rawSettings map[string]json.RawMessage
json.Unmarshal(data, &rawSettings)
permRaw, ok := rawSettings["permissions"]
if !ok { return }
var rawPermissions map[string]json.RawMessage
json.Unmarshal(permRaw, &rawPermissions)
if _, present := rawPermissions["deny"]; present { ... }
```

**Cost:** ~20 lines of hand-written read/parse code that every other test in the file avoids by calling the existing helper. It's also unnecessary: `testPermissions.Deny []string` (used by `readPermissions`) already distinguishes "key absent" (`nil`) from "key present as `[]`" (non-nil empty slice) under normal `encoding/json` unmarshal semantics, so the check this test needs is expressible as `perms.Deny != nil`.

```go
perms := readPermissions(t, tempDir)
if perms.Deny != nil {

}
```
using the existing `readPermissions` helper (same file, `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/hooks_test.go:255`).
